summary: First-contact record written by Mandel from a read-only reading of the session transcript and repository on 2026-10-20; the adversarial re-check of the headline numbers did not run (session limit), so every figure is the child's own and unverified. The child built a paper-first sports prediction and exchange-trading stack (sportsbot/: Elo/Markov models for tennis, MLB and table tennis, a Pinnacle-anchored sharp-line signal, Polymarket, Polymarket US and Kalshi clients, a tape-verified paper venue, a fail-closed risk layer and a tighten-only allocator) plus an independent dry-run engine suite, a shadow-mode certification engine and a Linode deployment, and then measured every strategy against the price it would have paid. Its own numbers say the models carry no information the venue lacks (Kalshi MLB: market Brier 0.2399 vs model 0.2422, beta 0.065, t 0.20, n 873; tennis bootstrap Brier 0.2589 vs market 0.2024 with bets losing ~18%), that pre-match moneylines are calibrated with no favourite-longshot edge after fees, that takers lose to makers (population CLV -0.0014 to -0.0033), that copying informed wallets nets -0.7 pt, that Polymarket follows Kalshi (t 4.4-5.3) but not by enough to take, and that seven candidate reference prices (NWS, sportsbook consensus, the other venue, the CPI nowcast, Deribit, spot vs Kalshi crypto hourlies, the index vs Kalshi index hourlies) do not lead their markets, leaving fed-funds futures vs Fed decision buckets as the only member and its G10 generalisation post hoc. The one positive, interval-bounded number is resting at the touch on slow team-sport books (+0.6 to +0.9c CLV per fill on MLB/NHL/NFL/CFB; Kalshi MLB +0.80c [+0.70, +0.92] net of maker fee at 120 s), which is a front-of-queue upper bound: counting the queue ahead on 16 NHL games it fills ~22% at -0.24 to -0.64 pt. It therefore pre-registered a $1-a-side live fill-share test (200 fills or 30 days; fund only if fill share x CLV clears the maker fee and the arm passes a 200-fill, CI-above-zero gate), rehearsed it in paper on Polymarket US (46 markets, 6 orders, one shadow bug found and fixed in PR #91), and is waiting on the operator's Polymarket US key. Paper book: $99.00 of $100.00, one settled bet, 18 resting orders a day with no tape fills; real book: $0, no keys in the repo, live needs both mode: live and SPORTSBOT_LIVE=1. It is unsure of the fill share, of Kalshi's maker fee per contract, of Polymarket US's live message format, and of whether the Fed/G10 rule survives a forward record; it holds that CLV against a sharp close is the only metric that can decide an edge within a season.
learnings: In-house rating models (MLB Elo + SP overlay, tennis Elo/Markov, table-tennis Elo) carry no information the venue price lacks; blending them in makes the market forecast worse. 'Calibrated is not the same as profitable.' | evidence: Result 2: beta 0.065, t 0.20, n 873 (Kalshi); Result 8: beta -0.95 to -0.62 (Polymarket, n 392-408); Results 5 and 9: tennis Brier 0.2589 vs 0.2024 and 0.2440 vs 0.2029; walk-forward, real quotes and fees, anchored on first pitch.

Pre-match sports moneylines on Polymarket and Kalshi are calibrated to within noise; there is no favorite-longshot edge after fees, and buying favorites loses 0.5-2% per $1 at every threshold before spread. | evidence: Result 6 (tennis within three points in every bucket, 3,122 side-observations; favorites -0.4% [-4.2%, +3.5%]); Result 9 (the +6% favourite cell was a final-volume look-ahead); docs/RESOLVED_MARKET_STUDY_2026-09-23.md.

Takers lose to makers as a population (about -0.15 to -0.33 pt CLV); informed taker flow exists (best-CLV wallets +1.0 pt out of sample) but copying it across the spread nets -0.7 pt; leaderboard (profit-ranked) wallets carry no information. | evidence: Result 14: 685 MLB markets, 760,382 taker fills, wallets ranked on first 70% of games and graded on the last 30%; tennis: nothing persists.

Resting at the touch on slow pre-game team-sport books (MLB, NHL, NFL, CFB) earns about +0.5-0.9 pt of CLV per fill IF the order is at the front of the queue; once the queue ahead is counted the edge is ~0 or negative (join: 22% filled at -0.24 to -0.64 pt). Only a live minimum-size order can measure the fill share. Tennis, esports and crypto windows: no touch edge. | evidence: Result 15 (+0.0070 [+0.0058, +0.0082], 182 markets), addendum 3 queue check (16 NHL games), Result 24 (Kalshi MLB front-of-queue +0.80c [+0.70, +0.92] vs strict +0.14c [-0.18, +0.47]), Result 19 (maker side +0.0015 [+0.0001, +0.0027] test), docs/MAKER_TEST.md pre-registered read-out (200 fills or 30 days; fill share x CLV must clear the maker fee and pass the gate).

Polymarket follows Kalshi (closing ~23% of a 0.6-pt gap in 90 s in active sessions, pooled t 4.4-5.3); Kalshi follows nothing; it is not a taker trade (-1.2 to -2.2 pt marked out) and cross-venue gaps above a few percent are suspect matches, not edges. | evidence: Result 10 and samples 1-17 (books every 20-30 s), docs/VENUE_LEAD_LAG_2026-09-23.md (148 matches), Result 11 (no cross-venue box in 156 pairs).

A 'reference price' beats a prediction market only when it is a deep market pricing the identical event against a thin crowd. One member (fed-funds futures vs Fed decision buckets); seven measured non-members: NWS weather, sportsbook consensus (soccer), Polymarket vs Kalshi, Cleveland Fed CPI nowcast, Deribit vs BTC/ETH digitals, Kalshi BTC/ETH hourlies vs spot, Kalshi S&P/Nasdaq hourlies vs the index. | evidence: Result 7 (beta 0.036), SPORTSBOOK_VS_POLYMARKET (1,048 matches), CPI study (0.018-0.029 Brier gap in the price's favour), CRYPTO_DERIBIT (17,425 digitals, diffs within +/-0.0002), 21d (328 events), Result 22 (5,597 events, pre-registered, t ~ 8).

Weather: the Kalshi daily-high market already contains the NWS forecast and beats it by an order of magnitude; our sigma is ~1.85x the bucket-implied sigma, so narrow centre buckets always look overpriced to us (a variance bet, not a temperature call). | evidence: 168 settled rows coin 0.2500 > climatology 0.1954 > NWS 0.1408 > market 0.0802; beta +0.036 [-0.106, +0.222]; 20 of 20 complete dates market wins; CLAUDE.md weather invariants; pre-live-gate skill check 8.

In-play MLB is not a feed race anyone outside the stadium wins: the venue covers half the move 6 s after the pitch, before MLB's own feed stamps the play; a zero-latency feed taker nets -0.16c per $1. | evidence: Result 23, 873 scoring plays in 198 games, CIs clustered by game; postseason -1.6c at 0 s.

Closing-line value against a sharp close (Pinnacle, Shin de-vigged, at >= 10 min lead) is the only evaluation metric that can decide an edge within a season; realised PnL from hundreds of bets cannot (2% ROI needs ~10,000 bets). | evidence: Power table in EDGE_VERDICT; docs/SHARP_CLV.md pre-registered pass (>= 1,000 graded decisions, taken-bet CLV > 0 with clustered CI excluding zero); literature (Data Golf 1:1 expected vs realised).

Literature synthesis: the only fee-inclusive edges against sports prices are structural (sharp-line fair value vs softer books +1.8-3.7% ROI decaying to +1.9%; decorrelated model +1.5-1.7 units/NBA season; Kalshi makers held to settlement +0.82-1.91c gross; favourite-side carry +2.6% for Kalshi makers above 50c); Vegas beat 538's MLB model over 25,165 games. | evidence: reports/Beating prediction market prices.md graded table (A/B/null) with sources; research_notes/.

Everything else measured loses its own costs: big pre-game moves followed or faded (-1.4 to -1.9 pt), fresh-wallet fade (holdout t 1.5, five markets), leaderboard wallets, crypto Up/Down maker pairs (0 of 701 unpaired legs won), complete-set/NegRisk arb after fees, order-book taker signals (information a third of the cost of taking). | evidence: Results 11-13, 18, 21a-c, taker retest 2026-10-14 (36 cells screened).
